Stated Claim / Post Context:
2 Franklin manufacturing facility employees treated for smoke inhalation after vacuum pump motor overheats

Two employees at a Franklin manufacturing facility were treated for smoke inhalation after a vacuum pump motor near the roof overheated on Thursday, according to the Franklin Fire Department.

Actual Article Body:
What This Story Is About

Why It Matters

What Happens Next

For Context

FRANKLIN, Tenn. (WSMV) - Two employees at a Franklin manufacturing facility were treated for smoke inhalation after a vacuum pump motor near the roof overheated on Thursday, according to the Franklin Fire Department.

FFD said crews responded to Lasko fan manufacturing facility on Confederate Drive for reports of a structure fire just after 10 a.m.

Fire Marshal Andy King said a vacuum pump motor near the roof overheated and caused a large amount of smoke to build up inside the facility.

“Employees used a dry chemical fire extinguisher on the overheated motor and began evacuating the facility,” FFD said.

The Franklin Fire Department was dispatched to a reported commercial structure fire at the Lasko fan manufacturing facility at 300 Confederate Drive today (10/29) at 10:08 AM.According to Fire Marshal Andy King, a vacuum pump motor near the roof overheated, producing a… pic.twitter.com/Mc6Ejm1XSu

When crews arrived, they found no active fire, but there was a significant amount of smoke in the building.

FFD said two employees were treated for smoke inhalation and taken to an area hospital by EMS.

“Firefighters remained on scene for more than an hour to ensure the building was safe,” FFD said.

The facility was closed for the remainder of the day as repairs were made.
